text.p: Here are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Slovenia will protest to Sir Arthur Watts, the mediator in ex-Yugoslavia's asset talks, about Yugoslavia's decision to privatise Slovenian assets in Yugoslavia.

- Slovenia plans to launch a complaint about a recent ruling by a Cypriot court concerning the division of money from former Yugoslavia that had been transferred to the Cypriot branch of Yugoslav bank Beogradska Banka.

- Slovenia's bid for non-permanent membership of the UN Security Council is supported by many western European countries, but that does not necessarily mean it will succeed, Slovenian diplomatic sources said.

- Almost 34 percent of Slovenians said they were worse off now than a year ago, 53.9 percent said they had the same standard of living as a year ago and 10.8 percent said they were better off now, an opinion poll said.
- The number of passengers crossing the Slovenian border in the first half of this year rose to 51.2 million, a 10 percent increase from the same period of 1996, the Statistical Office reported.
